objective: Define retained evidence versus disposable artifacts; expected: active output is never guessed stale.

governing_decision.section: Define stale output by ownership and use

decision: Every eligibility condition is required. Eligible output still requires immediate ownership/use recheck under the coordinator cleanup claim; the example never deletes files.
criteria: Approved build/temporary output root, regular known boundary
Terminal or confirmed abandoned owner; expired lease alone insufficient
No worker/evaluator/integrator/preview active or unknown use claim
Not retained verification evidence or latest verified build
At least 30 minutes since confirmed terminal/abandoned transition

existing_behavior.invariant: Held file is the capability; Drop retains ambiguous ownership; changed identity/bytes refuse release.

protected: shared caches without separate retention policy

alternatives.outcome: Rejected: active or retained evidence can be old.
Rejected: expiry does not establish process/use termination.

unresolved: No filesystem discovery or deleting cleanup executor is delivered by this design example.
No evidence that existing retained artifacts are currently stale is inferred.
Trusted claim collection, race-safe immediate coordinator cleanup and shared-cache retention remain their owning implementation tasks.
The pure example takes explicitly supplied facts; it does not authenticate or invent ownership.
